Meaning_EN: to arrive at (a conclusion) / to come to
Example_German: Nach langer Diskussion kamen wir zu einem Entschluss.
Example_English: After a long discussion we came to a decision.
Grammar_Notes: Often used with abstract nouns: zum Schluss kommen, zur Ruhe kommen.

Meaning_EN: to depend on / to be a matter of
Example_German: Es kommt auf das Wetter an, ob wir grillen.
Example_English: It depends on the weather whether we have a barbecue.
Grammar_Notes: Impersonal expression 'es kommt an auf...'. Synonymous with 'abhängen von'.

Meaning_EN: to think of / to hit upon (an idea or solution)
Example_German: Wie bist du denn auf diese geniale Idee gekommen?
Example_English: How did you come up with this brilliant idea?
Grammar_Notes: Idiomatic for suddenly getting an idea or remembering something.

Meaning_EN: to assume / to start from (a premise)
Example_German: Wir gehen von einem erfolgreichen Abschluss aus.
Example_English: We assume a successful conclusion.
Grammar_Notes: Very common in academic and formal German for stating assumptions.

Meaning_EN: to be about / to concern
Example_German: In diesem Film geht es um eine mutige Detektivin.
Example_English: This movie is about a courageous detective.
Grammar_Notes: Impersonal phrase: 'Es geht um + Akk.' Crucial for summarizing texts or plots.

Meaning_EN: to arise from / to develop out of
Example_German: Aus einem kleinen Missverständnis entstand aus der Streit.
Example_English: From a small misunderstanding arose the dispute.
Grammar_Notes: Indicates the source or root cause of a development.

Meaning_EN: to have an opinion on / to stand by
Example_German: Wie stehst du zu dem neuen Vorschlag?
Example_English: What is your stance on the new proposal?
Grammar_Notes: Expresses someone's attitude or commitment toward a topic or person.

Meaning_EN: to refrain from / to disregard
Example_German: Die Polizei sah diesmal von einer Geldstrafe ab.
Example_English: The police refrained from a fine this time.
Grammar_Notes: Often used in the fixed idiom 'abgesehen von + Dat' (apart from / aside from).

Meaning_EN: to regard as / to consider as
Example_German: Er sieht sie als seine beste Ratgeberin an.
Example_English: He regards her as his best advisor.
Grammar_Notes: 'Als' takes the same case as the object ('sie' = Akk -> 'seine beste Ratgeberin' = Akk).

Meaning_EN: to get involved in / to agree to (a venture or risk)
Example_German: Er wollte sich nicht auf dieses riskante Geschäft einlassen.
Example_English: He did not want to get involved in this risky business.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb (sich einlassen). Implies willingness to engage in something uncertain.

Meaning_EN: to have an opinion about / to reflect on
Example_German: Was denkst du eigentlich über seinen Vorschlag?
Example_English: What do you actually think about his proposal?
Grammar_Notes: Expresses an opinion or judgment (synonymous with 'meinen zu').

Meaning_EN: to ponder / to reflect on in depth
Example_German: Ich muss in Ruhe über dieses Angebot nachdenken.
Example_English: I need to reflect on this offer in peace.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb: implies deeper, continuous contemplation than 'denken an'.

Meaning_EN: to think of / to remember
Example_German: Ich muss jeden Tag an dich denken.
Example_English: I have to think of you every single day.
Grammar_Notes: Refers to having someone/something in mind, or remembering to do something.

Meaning_EN: to decrease in / to lose (quality/measure)
Example_German: Die Begeisterung nimmt leider an Intensität ab.
Example_English: The enthusiasm is unfortunately decreasing in intensity.

Meaning_EN: to increase in / to gain in
Example_German: Der Sturm nimmt stetig an Stärke zu.
Example_English: The storm is steadily increasing in strength.
Grammar_Notes: Used with abstract qualities: an Bedeutung zunehmen (gain importance).

Meaning_EN: to participate in / to take part in
Example_German: Viele Studenten nehmen an dem Sprachkurs teil.
Example_English: Many students take part in the language course.

Meaning_EN: to believe in
Example_German: Sie glaubt fest an das Gute im Menschen.
Example_English: She firmly believes in the good in people.
Grammar_Notes: Note: 'jemandem (Dat) glauben' means to believe someone's words; 'an + Akk glauben' means to have faith in.

Meaning_EN: to abide by / to adhere to (rules, agreements)
Example_German: Alle Autofahrer müssen sich an das Tempolimit halten.
Example_English: All drivers must adhere to the speed limit.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb (sich halten). Meaning: sticking strictly to a guideline.

Meaning_EN: to consider to be / to deem to be
Example_German: Ich halte diesen Plan für eine ausgezeichnete Idee.
Example_English: I consider this plan an excellent idea.
Grammar_Notes: Takes Akkusativ for both the direct object and the prepositional phrase.

Meaning_EN: to think of / to have an opinion of
Example_German: Was hältst du von meinem neuen Haarschnitt?
Example_English: What do you think of my new haircut?
Grammar_Notes: Standard conversational formula: 'Was hältst du von...?'

Meaning_EN: to deprive of / to rob someone of
Example_German: Der ständige Lärm bringt mich um den Schlaf.
Example_English: The constant noise robs me of my sleep.
Grammar_Notes: Idiom: 'jemanden um den Verstand / Schlaf bringen'.

Meaning_EN: to lead someone to / to prompt someone to
Example_German: Was hat dich zu dieser schweren Entscheidung gebracht?
Example_English: What prompted you to make this difficult decision?
Grammar_Notes: Often used with a direct object: jemanden zu etwas bringen.

Meaning_EN: to lead to / to result in
Example_German: Harte Arbeit führt oft zu großem Erfolg.
Example_English: Hard work often leads to great success.
Grammar_Notes: Cause-and-effect relationship. Very high frequency in writing.

Meaning_EN: to coordinate with / to agree on with
Example_German: Ich spreche den Urlaubsplan mit meinen Kollegen ab.
Example_English: I coordinate the vacation schedule with my colleagues.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb (ab|sprechen). To mutually arrange or agree.

Meaning_EN: to speak of / to mention / to tell of
Example_German: Mein Großvater spricht oft von seinen alten Freunden.
Example_English: My grandfather often speaks of his old friends.
Grammar_Notes: Focuses on referring to or recalling someone or an experience.

Meaning_EN: to speak with / to converse with
Example_German: Hast du schon mit deiner Lehrerin gesprochen?
Example_English: Have you already spoken with your teacher?
Grammar_Notes: Always takes 'mit + Dativ' for the conversational partner.

Meaning_EN: to talk about (a topic/subject)
Example_German: Wir müssen dringend über unsere Zukunft sprechen.
Example_English: We urgently need to talk about our future.
Grammar_Notes: Focuses on the content of the conversation.

Meaning_EN: to point at / to
Example_German: Das kleine Kind zeigte auf den bunten Schmetterling.
Example_English: The little child pointed at the colorful butterfly.
Grammar_Notes: Physical pointing gesture with finger or indicator.

Meaning_EN: to live for (a passion, purpose)
Example_German: Sie lebt ganz für ihre Musik und ihre Kunst.
Example_English: She lives entirely for her music and her art.
Grammar_Notes: Expresses true life dedication or passion.

Meaning_EN: to live on / to subsist on
Example_German: Er kann kaum von seinem geringen Einkommen leben.
Example_English: He can barely live on his meager income.

Meaning_EN: to travel by / to ride with (means of transport)
Example_German: Morgens fahre ich am liebsten mit der U-Bahn.
Example_English: In the morning I prefer traveling by subway.
Grammar_Notes: All vehicles in German take 'mit + Dativ' (mit dem Bus, mit dem Zug).

Meaning_EN: to ask about / to inquire after
Example_German: Ein Tourist fragte mich nach dem kürzesten Weg zum Bahnhof.
Example_English: A tourist asked me for the shortest way to the station.
Grammar_Notes: Standard formula: jemanden (Akk) nach etwas (Dat) fragen.

Meaning_EN: to ask for (advice / help)
Example_German: Sie fragte ihren Mentor um Rat in dieser Angelegenheit.
Example_English: She asked her mentor for advice in this matter.
Grammar_Notes: Most commonly in the fixed idiom 'um Rat fragen'.

Meaning_EN: to apply to / to be valid for
Example_German: Diese Sonderregelung gilt nur für neue Kunden.
Example_English: This special regulation applies only to new customers.
Grammar_Notes: Denotes the scope of validity of rules, laws, tickets.

Meaning_EN: to be considered as / to count as
Example_German: Er gilt weltweit als führender Experte für KI.
Example_English: He is considered worldwide as a leading expert in AI.
Grammar_Notes: 'Als' takes Nominative when referring to the grammatical subject.

Meaning_EN: to adapt to / to prepare oneself for
Example_German: Wir müssen uns auf plötzliche Veränderungen einstellen.
Example_English: We must adapt to sudden changes.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb (sich einstellen auf). Mentally getting ready for something.

Meaning_EN: to play for (money, stakes, championship)
Example_German: Die beiden Teams spielen um den Meistertitel.
Example_English: Both teams are playing for the championship title.
Grammar_Notes: Specifies the prize or stake at risk in a game.

Meaning_EN: to play with
Example_German: Die Katze spielt begeistert mit dem Wollknäuel.
Example_English: The cat enthusiastically plays with the ball of yarn.
Grammar_Notes: Literal or figurative ('mit dem Feuer spielen' = to play with fire).

Meaning_EN: to work at / for (an employer or company)
Example_German: Mein Bruder arbeitet schon seit fünf Jahren bei BMW.
Example_English: My brother has been working at BMW for five years.
Grammar_Notes: Used for the company/institution that employs someone.

Meaning_EN: to work for (a client, employer, or cause)
Example_German: Sie arbeitet als freie Journalistin für verschiedene Zeitungen.
Example_English: She works as a freelance journalist for various newspapers.
Grammar_Notes: Emphasizes the beneficiary or contracting party.

Meaning_EN: to work on (a project, task, book)
Example_German: Die Wissenschaftler arbeiten an einem neuen Impfstoff.
Example_English: The scientists are working on a new vaccine.
Grammar_Notes: Always Dativ when indicating the task or project being worked upon.

Meaning_EN: to follow from / to result from
Example_German: Aus dieser Analyse folgt aus den Daten eine klare Warnung.
Example_English: From this analysis, a clear warning follows from the data.

Meaning_EN: to learn from (a mistake, experience)
Example_German: Kluge Menschen lernen aus ihren eigenen Fehlern.
Example_English: Smart people learn from their own mistakes.
Grammar_Notes: Indicates the source of wisdom or lesson.

Meaning_EN: to get along with (someone)
Example_German: Ich verstehe mich hervorragend mit meinem neuen Mitbewohner.
Example_English: I get along great with my new roommate.

Meaning_EN: to understand by (a concept or definition)
Example_German: Was verstehen Sie genau unter dem Begriff Nachhaltigkeit?
Example_English: What exactly do you understand by the concept of sustainability?
Grammar_Notes: Used when asking for definitions or subjective interpretations.

Meaning_EN: to advocate for / to champion / to stand up for
Example_German: Die Organisation setzt sich entschlossen für den Tierschutz ein.
Example_English: The organization resolutely advocates for animal welfare.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb (sich einsetzen für). Dedicating active effort to a cause.

Meaning_EN: to deal with / to grapple with / to examine
Example_German: Der Philosoph setzt sich tiefgehend mit ethischen Fragen auseinander.
Example_English: The philosopher grapples profoundly with ethical questions.
Grammar_Notes: Crucial academic verb for critical engagement with a subject.

Meaning_EN: to begin with / to start with
Example_German: Wir beginnen die Besprechung mit einer kurzen Vorstellungsrunde.
Example_English: We start the meeting with a short round of introductions.

Meaning_EN: to tell / report about (factual topic or detailed info)
Example_German: Der Reiseleiter erzählte viel Interessantes über die alte Burg.
Example_English: The tour guide told many interesting things about the old castle.
Grammar_Notes: 'über + Akk' focuses on specific facts/details of a subject.

Meaning_EN: to tell about / to narrate (events or experiences)
Example_German: Oma erzählte uns stundenlang von ihrer Jugend auf dem Land.
Example_English: Grandma told us for hours about her youth in the countryside.
Grammar_Notes: General recounting of memories or stories.

Meaning_EN: to work on writing (a book, dissertation, article)
Example_German: Der bekannte Schriftsteller schreibt schon seit Jahren an einem neuen Roman.
Example_English: The famous author has been working on writing a new novel for years.
Grammar_Notes: Note the contrast: 'an + Dat' means being in the process of composing a work!

Meaning_EN: to write about (a topic)
Example_German: Er schreibt seine Masterarbeit über erneuerbare Energien.
Example_English: He is writing his master's thesis about renewable energy.
Grammar_Notes: Denotes the theme or topic of the written piece.

Meaning_EN: to write to (a recipient)
Example_German: Sie schreibt eine lange Nachricht an ihre beste Freundin.
Example_English: She is writing a long message to her best friend.
Grammar_Notes: Recipient takes Akkusativ: 'an + Akk' (alternatively just Dativ without prep).

Meaning_EN: to be a matter of / to concern (essential nature)
Example_German: Bei dieser Angelegenheit handelt es sich um ein ernstes Problem.
Example_English: In this matter, it is a serious problem.
Grammar_Notes: Impersonal reflexive: always 'es handelt sich um + Akk'. Used for formal definitions.

Meaning_EN: to be about (plot, theme of a story/book/movie)
Example_German: Das Lied handelt von einer bittersüßen Liebe im Sommer.
Example_English: The song is about a bittersweet love in summer.
Grammar_Notes: Active verb: 'Das Buch handelt von...'. Do not confuse with 'es handelt sich um'!

Meaning_EN: to trade in / to deal with (goods, commodities)
Example_German: Der Händler handelt mit edlen Weinen und Antiquitäten.
Example_English: The merchant trades in fine wines and antiques.

Meaning_EN: to belong to / to be part of (a group, set, or category)
Example_German: Kaffee gehört für viele zu einem perfekten Morgen.
Example_English: For many, coffee belongs to a perfect morning.
Grammar_Notes: Membership or integral part. Note: simple ownership is 'etwas gehört jemandem (Dat)' without prep.

Meaning_EN: to ask for / to request
Example_German: Darf ich Sie um einen kurzen Augenblick Geduld bitten?
Example_English: May I ask you for a brief moment of patience?
Grammar_Notes: Formula: jemanden (Akk) um etwas (Akk) bitten. Crucial polite request phrasing.

Meaning_EN: to hold off on / to delay doing something
Example_German: Wir sollten mit dem Kauf noch warten, bis die Preise sinken.
Example_English: We should hold off on the purchase until prices drop.
Grammar_Notes: Indicates postponing an action: 'mit der Entscheidung warten'.

Meaning_EN: to wait for
Example_German: Wir warten schon seit einer halben Stunde auf den verspäteten Zug.
Example_English: We have been waiting for the delayed train for half an hour.
Grammar_Notes: Preposition 'auf' always takes Akkusativ here. Never use 'für'!

Meaning_EN: to consist in / to lie in (the essence of)
Example_German: Die Schwierigkeit besteht in der genauen Umsetzung des Plans.
Example_English: The difficulty lies in the exact implementation of the plan.
Grammar_Notes: Defines the core essence or nature of an abstract issue.

Meaning_EN: to consist of / to be made of
Example_German: Das Team besteht aus fünf erfahrenen Entwicklern.
Example_English: The team consists of five experienced developers.

Meaning_EN: to insist on
Example_German: Der Gast bestand unnachgiebig auf seinem Recht auf Rückerstattung.
Example_English: The guest unyieldingly insisted on his right to a refund.
Grammar_Notes: In modern German, 'bestehen auf' predominantly takes Dativ.

Meaning_EN: to search for / to look for
Example_German: Die Forscher suchen intensiv nach einer Heilung für die Krankheit.
Example_English: The researchers are searching intensively for a cure for the disease.
Grammar_Notes: Note: 'etwas suchen' (direct object Akk) is common for objects; 'suchen nach + Dat' emphasizes ongoing quest/effort.

Meaning_EN: to hope for
Example_German: Die Landwirte hoffen dringend auf ergiebigen Regen.
Example_English: The farmers are urgently hoping for plentiful rain.

Meaning_EN: to pay attention to / to watch out for
Example_German: Beim Überqueren der Straße musst du auf den Verkehr achten.
Example_English: When crossing the street you have to pay attention to the traffic.
Grammar_Notes: Active attentiveness or care (e.g. auf die Ernährung achten).

Meaning_EN: to reply to / to answer (a question or message)
Example_German: Er hat noch immer nicht auf meine dringende Frage geantwortet.
Example_English: He still hasn't answered my urgent question.
Grammar_Notes: jemandem (Dat) auf etwas (Akk) antworten. Contrast: 'etwas beantworten' takes direct Akk object.

Meaning_EN: to thank for
Example_German: Ich danke dir von ganzem Herzen für deine großzügige Unterstützung.
Example_English: I thank you with all my heart for your generous support.

Meaning_EN: to count on / to expect / to anticipate
Example_German: Im Winter muss man jederzeit mit glatten Straßen rechnen.
Example_English: In winter one must expect slippery roads at any time.
Grammar_Notes: Anticipating a condition, event, or problem.

Meaning_EN: to lack / to be deficient in
Example_German: In dem Projekt fehlt es vor allem an qualifizierten Mitarbeitern.
Example_English: In the project, there is primarily a lack of qualified employees.
Grammar_Notes: Often used impersonally: 'Es fehlt an + Dat'.

Meaning_EN: to fit onto / to fit (physically)
Example_German: Der Deckel passt genau auf diese kleine Dose.
Example_English: The lid fits exactly onto this small tin.
Grammar_Notes: Physical fit or attachment onto a surface/opening.

Meaning_EN: to match / to suit / to go well with
Example_German: Dieser dunkle Gürtel passt perfekt zu deinen neuen Schuhen.
Example_English: This dark belt goes perfectly with your new shoes.
Grammar_Notes: Compatibility in style, character, or harmony.

Meaning_EN: to trust in / to rely on
Example_German: Sie vertraut voll und ganz auf ihre eigene Intuition.
Example_English: She trusts completely in her own intuition.
Grammar_Notes: Can take simple Dativ (jemandem vertrauen) or 'auf + Akk' for strong reliance/faith.

Meaning_EN: to suffer from (a specific medical illness or disease)
Example_German: Der Patient leidet seit seiner Kindheit an schwerem Asthma.
Example_English: The patient has suffered from severe asthma since childhood.
Grammar_Notes: CRUCIAL CONTRAST: 'leiden an + Dat' is reserved for diagnostic illnesses/diseases.

Meaning_EN: to suffer under (difficult circumstances, stress, noise, loneliness)
Example_German: Viele Großstädter leiden unter dem ständigen Lärm und der Hektik.
Example_English: Many city dwellers suffer under the constant noise and hectic pace.
Grammar_Notes: CRUCIAL CONTRAST: 'leiden unter + Dat' is used for environmental or situational conditions.

Meaning_EN: to doubt / to have doubts about
Example_German: Niemand im Kollegium zweifelt an seiner außergewöhnlichen Kompetenz.
Example_English: No one on the faculty doubts his extraordinary competence.

Meaning_EN: to be pleased / happy about (a PRESENT or PAST event/gift)
Example_German: Ich habe mich sehr über deinen liebevollen Brief gefreut.
Example_English: I was very pleased about your loving letter.
Grammar_Notes: PRESENT/PAST ONLY: reaction to something that has occurred or already arrived.

Meaning_EN: to look forward to (a FUTURE event)
Example_German: Wir freuen uns schon riesig auf den bevorstehenden Urlaub.
Example_English: We are already looking forward very much to the upcoming vacation.
Grammar_Notes: FUTURE TIME ONLY: anticipation of something yet to happen. Always Akkusativ.

Meaning_EN: to be interested in
Example_German: Interessierst du dich eigentlich für klassische Architektur?
Example_English: Are you actually interested in classical architecture?
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb with Akk. object (sich) and 'für + Akk'.

Meaning_EN: to remember / to recall
Example_German: Erinnert ihr euch noch an unseren ersten gemeinsamen Schultag?
Example_English: Do you still remember our first school day together?
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive: 'sich erinnern an + Akk'. Active form 'jemanden an etwas erinnern' = to remind someone of something.

Meaning_EN: to take care of / to look after / to attend to
Example_German: Wer kümmert sich während deiner Abwesenheit um die Haustiere?
Example_English: Who will take care of the pets during your absence?
Grammar_Notes: Taking responsibility for someone or dealing with a task.

Meaning_EN: to be annoyed / irritated / angry about
Example_German: Sie ärgert sich maßlos über den unzuverlässigen Handwerker.
Example_English: She is exceedingly annoyed about the unreliable craftsman.

Meaning_EN: to occupy oneself with / to be busy with
Example_German: In ihrer Freizeit beschäftigt sie sich gern mit Malerei.
Example_English: In her free time she likes to occupy herself with painting.
Grammar_Notes: Dedicated activity or hobby. Always takes 'mit + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to apply for (a job, position, scholarship)
Example_German: Er bewirbt sich um ein Stipendium an einer angesehenen Universität.
Example_English: He is applying for a scholarship at a prestigious university.
Grammar_Notes: The target role or prize takes 'um + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to apply to / at (a company, institution)
Example_German: Sie hat sich bei einer internationalen Bank beworben.
Example_English: She applied at an international bank.

Meaning_EN: to get used to / to accustom oneself to
Example_German: Ich kann mich einfach nicht an den frühen Wecker gewöhnen.
Example_English: I simply cannot get used to the early alarm clock.

Meaning_EN: to concentrate on / to focus on
Example_German: Bitte konzentrieren Sie sich voll auf die bevorstehende Prüfung!
Example_English: Please concentrate fully on the upcoming exam!
Grammar_Notes: Direction of mental focus: takes Akkusativ.

Meaning_EN: to rely on / to depend on
Example_German: Auf meine engsten Freunde kann ich mich immer auf blind verlassen.
Example_English: I can always blindly rely on my closest friends.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive verb (sich verlassen auf). Trusting someone's dependability.

Meaning_EN: to refer to / to relate to
Example_German: Mein Schreiben bezieht sich auf Ihr Inserat vom 15. Mai.
Example_English: My letter refers to your advertisement from May 15th.
Grammar_Notes: Essential in formal correspondence ('Bezug nehmend auf...').

Meaning_EN: to prepare for
Example_German: Die Sportler bereiten sich monatelang auf den Marathon vor.
Example_English: The athletes prepare for months for the marathon.

Meaning_EN: to fall in love with
Example_German: Er hat sich unsterblich in seine Arbeitskollegin verliebt.
Example_English: He fell hopelessly in love with his coworker.

Meaning_EN: to arrange to meet with / to make a date with
Example_German: Ich habe mich für heute Abend mit Markus verabredet.
Example_English: I arranged to meet with Markus for this evening.

Meaning_EN: to depend on
Example_German: Der Erfolg eines Unternehmens hängt stark von seinen Mitarbeitern ab.
Example_English: The success of a business depends heavily on its employees.

Meaning_EN: to stop / to cease doing something
Example_German: Wann hörst du endlich mit dem ständigen Jammern auf?
Example_English: When will you finally stop the constant whining?

Meaning_EN: to watch out for / to look after
Example_German: Könntest du kurz auf mein Gepäck aufpassen?
Example_English: Could you watch my luggage for a moment?
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb: 'auf|passen auf + Akk'. Guarding or minding someone/something.

Meaning_EN: to spend (money) on
Example_German: Er gibt viel zu viel Geld für teure Kleidung aus.
Example_English: He spends far too much money on expensive clothes.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb: Geld ausgeben für + Akk.

Meaning_EN: to contribute to
Example_German: Jeder einzelne Bürger kann zu einer sauberen Umwelt beitragen.
Example_English: Every single citizen can contribute to a clean environment.
Grammar_Notes: Irregular separable verb (trägt bei; trug bei; beigetragen).

Meaning_EN: to report / tell of (an incident or experience)
Example_German: Der Augenzeuge berichtete von einem lauten Knall.
Example_English: The eyewitness reported of a loud bang.
Grammar_Notes: Focuses on personal observation or occurrence.

Meaning_EN: to report on (a comprehensive subject or event)
Example_German: Die Zeitungen berichten ausführlich über die neue Gesetzesreform.
Example_English: The newspapers report extensively on the new legal reform.

Meaning_EN: to invite to (an event or party)
Example_German: Wir möchten dich herzlich zu unserer Geburtstagsfeier einladen.
Example_English: We would like to warmly invite you to our birthday party.

Meaning_EN: to decide against
Example_German: Er hat sich bewusst gegen den teuren Umzug entschieden.
Example_English: He deliberately decided against the expensive relocation.

Meaning_EN: to decide in favor of / to choose
Example_German: Nach langer Überlegung entschied sie sich für das Medizinstudium.
Example_English: After long consideration she decided in favor of medical school.

Meaning_EN: to apologize for (a mistake or action)
Example_German: Ich entschuldige mich vielmals für das Missgeschick.
Example_English: I apologize very much for the mishap.
Grammar_Notes: The reason for the apology takes 'für + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to apologize to (a person)
Example_German: Er sollte sich aufrichtig bei seiner Nachbarin entschuldigen.
Example_English: He should sincerely apologize to his neighbor.
Grammar_Notes: The recipient of the apology takes 'bei + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to recover from (illness, stress, strain)
Example_German: Sie muss sich erst von den Strapazen der langen Reise erholen.
Example_English: She first needs to recover from the hardships of the long journey.

Meaning_EN: to recognize by (a characteristic feature)
Example_German: Ich habe sie sofort an ihrem herzlichen Lachen erkannt.
Example_English: I recognized her immediately by her hearty laugh.

Meaning_EN: to inquire about (information, conditions)
Example_German: Er erkundigte sich am Schalter nach den Abfahrtszeiten.
Example_English: He inquired at the counter about departure times.
Grammar_Notes: More formal synonym for 'fragen nach + Dat'.

Meaning_EN: to inquire with / at (a person or institution)
Example_German: Sie erkundigte sich bei der Behörde nach den notwendigen Unterlagen.
Example_English: She inquired at the agency about the required documents.
Grammar_Notes: The source/authority being asked takes 'bei + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to be frightened of (a sudden noise, animal, entity)
Example_German: Das Baby erschrak furchtbar vor dem lauten Donner.
Example_English: The baby was terribly frightened by the loud thunder.
Grammar_Notes: Direct sensory startle response to a danger or sudden noise.

Meaning_EN: to be shocked / startled by (news, realization)
Example_German: Die Bürger erschraken über den drastischen Preisanstieg.
Example_English: The citizens were shocked by the drastic price increase.
Grammar_Notes: Emotional shock upon discovering a fact or news item.

Meaning_EN: to be afraid of / to dread
Example_German: Manche Menschen fürchten sich vor engen Räumen.
Example_English: Some people are afraid of confined spaces.
Grammar_Notes: Always 'vor + Dativ'. Synonymous with 'Angst haben vor + Dat'.

Meaning_EN: to congratulate on
Example_German: Wir gratulieren dir ganz herzlich zu deiner bestandenen Prüfung!
Example_English: We warmly congratulate you on your passed exam!

Meaning_EN: to complain about / to lament
Example_German: Die Patienten klagen über anhaltende Übelkeit.
Example_English: The patients complain of persistent nausea.

Meaning_EN: to file a lawsuit against / to sue
Example_German: Der Anwohner klagt gegen den Bau der neuen Autobahn.
Example_English: The resident is suing against the construction of the new highway.
Grammar_Notes: Legal context: bringing action before a court.

Meaning_EN: to protest against
Example_German: Tausende Bürger protestieren friedlich gegen die Steuererhöhung.
Example_English: Thousands of citizens are peacefully protesting against the tax increase.

Meaning_EN: to react to
Example_German: Wie hat die Schulleitung auf die Beschwerde reagiert?
Example_English: How did the school administration react to the complaint?

Meaning_EN: to smell like / of
Example_German: Im ganzen Haus riecht es köstlich nach frisch gebackenem Brot.
Example_English: The whole house smells delicious like freshly baked bread.

Meaning_EN: to taste like / of
Example_German: Das Dessert schmeckt wunderbar nach frischer Vanille.
Example_English: The dessert tastes wonderful like fresh vanilla.

Meaning_EN: to protect against (disease, attack)
Example_German: Die Impfung schützt zuverlässig gegen eine schwere Infektion.
Example_English: The vaccination reliably protects against severe infection.
Grammar_Notes: Often used interchangeably with 'vor + Dat', especially in medical contexts.

Meaning_EN: to protect from / to shield against
Example_German: Sonnencreme schützt die empfindliche Haut vor gefährlichen Sonnenbränden.
Example_English: Sunscreen protects sensitive skin from dangerous sunburns.
Grammar_Notes: Defense against an environmental threat or hazard.

Meaning_EN: to provide for / to ensure / to take care of
Example_German: Gute Musik sorgt für eine ausgelassene Stimmung.
Example_English: Good music provides for a lively atmosphere.
Grammar_Notes: Creating a condition or caring for dependents ('für die Kinder sorgen').

Meaning_EN: to worry about
Example_German: Die Großmutter sorgt sich sehr um das Wohl ihrer Enkel.
Example_English: The grandmother worries greatly about the well-being of her grandchildren.
Grammar_Notes: Reflexive: 'sich sorgen um + Akk'. Synonymous with 'sich Sorgen machen um'.

Meaning_EN: to die of (a cause or illness)
Example_German: Viele Patienten starben früher an einer einfachen Wundinfektion.
Example_English: Many patients formerly died of a simple wound infection.

Meaning_EN: to dream of / about
Example_German: Seit ihrer Kindheit träumt sie von einem eigenen Haus am Meer.
Example_English: Since childhood she has been dreaming of her own house by the sea.
Grammar_Notes: Both nocturnal dreams and long-term aspirational wishes.

Meaning_EN: to convince of / to persuade of
Example_German: Seine schlüssigen Argumente überzeugten uns von der Richtigkeit des Plans.
Example_English: His coherent arguments convinced us of the correctness of the plan.

Meaning_EN: to converse about / to discuss (a topic)
Example_German: Wir haben uns stundenlang über alte Erinnerungen unterhalten.
Example_English: We chatted for hours about old memories.

Meaning_EN: to converse with / to chat with (someone)
Example_German: Ich habe mich auf dem Empfang lange mit dem Botschafter unterhalten.
Example_English: At the reception, I chatted for a long time with the ambassador.

Meaning_EN: to connect with / to associate with
Example_German: Mit diesem melancholischen Lied verbinde ich mit meinen schönsten Sommer.
Example_English: I associate this melancholic song with my most beautiful summer.

Meaning_EN: to compare with
Example_German: Man kann die Situation heute kaum mit den Zuständen vor fünfzig Jahren vergleichen.
Example_English: One can hardly compare the situation today with conditions fifty years ago.

Meaning_EN: to do without / to forgo / to renounce
Example_German: Er verzichtet während der Fastenzeit komplett auf raffinierten Zucker.
Example_English: During Lent, he completely gives up refined sugar.
Grammar_Notes: Voluntarily giving up a privilege, habit, or item. Always 'auf + Akk'.

Meaning_EN: to warn against / to alert to
Example_German: Experten warnen eindringlich vor den Folgen des Klimawandels.
Example_English: Experts urgently warn against the consequences of climate change.

Meaning_EN: to be surprised at / to wonder at
Example_German: Ich wundere mich immer wieder über seine unglaubliche Energie.
Example_English: I am repeatedly amazed at his incredible energy.

Meaning_EN: to be connected with / to correlate with
Example_German: Häufige Kopfschmerzen hängen oft eng mit zu wenig Schlaf zusammen.
Example_English: Frequent headaches are often closely linked to too little sleep.

Meaning_EN: to force to / to compel to
Example_German: Die schwere Verletzung zwang den Athleten zu einem vorzeitigen Karriereende.
Example_English: The severe injury forced the athlete to an early retirement.

Meaning_EN: to start with / to begin with
Example_German: Wann fängst du endlich mit der Vorbereitung auf das Examen an?
Example_English: When will you finally start preparing for the exam?
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb (fängt an; fing an; angefangen). Takes Dativ.

Meaning_EN: to address / to respond to / to agree to
Example_German: Der Referent ging freundlich auf alle Fragen des Publikums ein.
Example_English: The speaker kindly addressed all questions from the audience.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb (auf etwas eingehen). Thorough response or consideration.

Meaning_EN: to point out / to draw attention to
Example_German: Das Schild weist die Autofahrer auf die akute Rutschgefahr hin.
Example_English: The sign alerts drivers to the acute danger of skidding.

Meaning_EN: to hear from / about (someone/something)
Example_German: Hast du in letzter Zeit etwas Neues von deinem Schulfreund gehört?
Example_English: Have you heard anything new from your school friend lately?

Meaning_EN: to listen to / to obey (advice, a person)
Example_German: Der sture Junge will einfach nicht auf den Rat seiner Eltern hören.
Example_English: The stubborn boy simply does not want to listen to his parents' advice.

Meaning_EN: to fight against (an enemy, injustice, disease)
Example_German: Die Ärzte kämpfen mit allen Mitteln gegen die heimtückische Krankheit.
Example_English: Doctors are fighting by all means against the insidious disease.

Meaning_EN: to fight for (a cause, justice, freedom)
Example_German: Aktivisten kämpfen unermüdlich für eine gerechtere Welt.
Example_English: Activists fight tirelessly for a more just world.
Grammar_Notes: Fighting in support of a goal.

Meaning_EN: to fight over / for (survival, a trophy, custody)
Example_German: Die beiden Finalisten kämpfen verbissen um den begehrten Pokal.
Example_English: Both finalists are fighting fiercely for the coveted trophy.
Grammar_Notes: Contesting or struggling to obtain/retain an object or state.

Meaning_EN: to cope with / to manage / to get along with
Example_German: Kommst du im Alltag gut mit deinem neuen Vorgesetzten klar?
Example_English: Do you get along well with your new supervisor in daily life?

Meaning_EN: to lack / to be wanting in
Example_German: Dem jungen Start-up mangelt es vor allem an ausreichendem Kapital.
Example_English: The young start-up primarily lacks sufficient capital.
Grammar_Notes: Impersonal: 'Es mangelt an + Dat'. Similar to 'fehlen an'.

Meaning_EN: to profit from / to benefit from
Example_German: Beide Unternehmen profitieren enorm von der neuen Partnerschaft.
Example_English: Both companies benefit enormously from the new partnership.
Grammar_Notes: Gaining an advantage from a situation.

Meaning_EN: to take revenge for (an offense or wrong)
Example_German: Sie wollte sich für die schwere Demütigung rächen.
Example_English: She wanted to avenge the severe humiliation.
Grammar_Notes: The reason or grievance takes 'für + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to take revenge on (a person)
Example_German: Er schwor, sich eines Tages an seinem Verräter zu rächen.
Example_English: He swore to take revenge on his betrayer one day.
Grammar_Notes: The target of revenge takes 'an + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to advise to / to recommend
Example_German: Der Arzt riet ihm dringend zu einer sofortigen Kur.
Example_English: The doctor urgently advised him to take an immediate spa cure.

Meaning_EN: to address to / to direct toward (an audience)
Example_German: Die Worte der Kanzlerin richteten sich an das gesamte Volk.
Example_English: The Chancellor's words were addressed to the entire nation.

Meaning_EN: to conform to / to be guided by / to depend on
Example_German: Der genaue Preis richtet sich nach der gewünschten Ausstattung.
Example_English: The exact price depends on the desired equipment.

Meaning_EN: to rant about / to grumble about
Example_German: Die Pendler schimpfen täglich über die unpünktlichen Züge.
Example_English: Commuters rant daily about the unpunctual trains.

Meaning_EN: to scold / to tell off (a person)
Example_German: Die Mutter schimpfte mit ihrem unartigen Sohn.
Example_English: The mother scolded her naughty son.

Meaning_EN: to deduce from / to conclude from
Example_German: Aus diesen Befunden schließt der Ermittler aus den genauen Tathergang.
Example_English: From these findings, the investigator deduces the exact sequence of events.

Meaning_EN: to long for / to yearn for
Example_German: Im kalten und dunklen Winter sehnt er sich nach Wärme und Licht.
Example_English: In the cold and dark winter, he yearns for warmth and light.

Meaning_EN: to triumph over / to defeat
Example_German: Am Ende siegte die Gerechtigkeit über die Willkür.
Example_English: In the end, justice triumphed over arbitrariness.
Grammar_Notes: Victory over an adversary or difficulty.

Meaning_EN: to vote against
Example_German: Nur zwei Parteimitglieder stimmten gegen den Beschluss.
Example_English: Only two party members voted against the resolution.

Meaning_EN: to vote in favor of
Example_German: Die Abgeordneten stimmten mit großer Mehrheit für den Gesetzentwurf.
Example_English: The deputies voted by a large majority in favor of the bill.

Meaning_EN: to argue / quarrel about (a topic)
Example_German: Die Politiker streiten leidenschaftlich über die richtige Steuerreform.
Example_English: The politicians are passionately arguing about the right tax reform.
Grammar_Notes: Topic of the dispute takes 'über + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to argue with (a person)
Example_German: Ich habe keine Lust, mich ständig mit dir zu streiten.
Example_English: I have no desire to constantly argue with you.
Grammar_Notes: Opponent in the dispute takes 'mit + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to dispute over / to contest (property, possession)
Example_German: Die zerstrittenen Geschwister streiten um das Erbe der Eltern.
Example_English: The estranged siblings are quarreling over the parents' inheritance.
Grammar_Notes: Contesting ownership or control of an asset.

Meaning_EN: to be fit for / to be good for
Example_German: Dieses alte, stumpfe Messer taugt nicht mehr zu Schneiden von Fleisch.
Example_English: This old, blunt knife is no longer good for cutting meat.

Meaning_EN: to persuade into / to talk someone into
Example_German: Sie überredete ihren Freund zu einem gemeinsamen Tanzkurs.
Example_English: She talked her boyfriend into taking a dance course together.

Meaning_EN: to judge according to / by
Example_German: Man darf Personen niemals nur nach ihrem äußeren Anschein beurteilen.
Example_English: One must never judge persons solely by their outward appearance.
Grammar_Notes: The criteria or basis of judgment takes 'nach + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to pass judgment on / to judge
Example_German: Niemand sollte vorschnell über andere Menschen urteilen.
Example_English: Nobody should judge other people hastily.
Grammar_Notes: Making an evaluation or moral assessment.

Meaning_EN: to entice / seduce into
Example_German: Die ständigen Sonderangebote verführten ihn zu unnötigen Ausgaben.
Example_English: The constant special offers seduced him into unnecessary spending.
Grammar_Notes: Tempting someone to do something unwise or illicit.

Meaning_EN: to negotiate about (wages, conditions)
Example_German: Die Gewerkschaft verhandelt derzeit über eine spürbare Lohnerhöhung.
Example_English: The union is currently negotiating for a noticeable pay raise.

Meaning_EN: to negotiate with (a party, representative)
Example_German: Die Firmenleitung verhandelt direkt mit dem Betriebsrat.
Example_English: Management is negotiating directly with the works council.

Meaning_EN: to crave / to call for / to yearn for
Example_German: Nach stundenlanger Wanderung in der Hitze verlangte sein Körper nach kaltem Wasser.
Example_English: After hours of hiking in the heat, his body craved cold water.
Grammar_Notes: Strong physical or psychological craving. Always 'nach + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to violate / to offend against (laws, regulations)
Example_German: Dieses illegale Verhalten verstößt eindeutig gegen geltendes Recht.
Example_English: This illegal behavior clearly violates applicable law.
Grammar_Notes: Breaching rules or ethical codes. Always 'gegen + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to immerse oneself in / to become engrossed in
Example_German: Sie vertiefte sich völlig in das fesselnde Geschichtsbuch.
Example_English: She immersed herself completely in the captivating history book.
Grammar_Notes: Total absorption in study or reading. Takes 'in + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: to elect as / to choose as
Example_German: Die Mitglieder wählten sie einstimmig zu neuen Vorsitzenden.
Example_English: The members unanimously elected her as the new chairperson.

Meaning_EN: to turn against / to oppose
Example_German: Die öffentliche Kritik wendet sich nun scharf gegen die Entscheidungsträger.
Example_English: Public criticism is now turning sharply against the decision-makers.
Grammar_Notes: Taking an adversarial stance against someone/something.

Meaning_EN: to turn to / to consult / to contact
Example_German: Bei rechtlichen Fragen sollten Sie sich sofort an einen Fachanwalt wenden.
Example_English: For legal questions you should immediately turn to a specialist lawyer.
Grammar_Notes: Seeking assistance or counsel from someone.

Meaning_EN: to advertise / to promote / to campaign for
Example_German: Das Unternehmen wirbt intensiv für seine neue Produktlinie.
Example_English: The company advertises intensively for its new product line.
Grammar_Notes: Commercial promotion or advocating an idea.

Meaning_EN: to court / to solicit / to vie for
Example_German: Internationale Universitäten werben eifrig um talentierte Nachwuchsforscher.
Example_English: International universities eagerly vie for talented young researchers.

Meaning_EN: to have an effect on / to make an impression on
Example_German: Die sanfte Melodie wirkt überaus beruhigend auf gestresste Gemüter.
Example_English: The gentle melody has an exceedingly calming effect on stressed minds.
Grammar_Notes: Psychological or physical effect on someone.

Meaning_EN: to count among / to rank among
Example_German: Diese Entdeckung zählt zweifellos zu den größten Meilensteinen der Medizin.
Example_English: This discovery undoubtedly counts among the greatest milestones in medicine.

Meaning_EN: to count on / to rely on
Example_German: In schwierigen Zeiten kann ich mich immer auf meine treuen Freunde verlassen und auf sie zählen.
Example_English: In difficult times I can always count on my loyal friends.

Meaning_EN: to hesitate with / to delay doing
Example_German: Bitte zögern Sie nicht mit Ihrer Rückmeldung!
Example_English: Please do not hesitate with your feedback!
Grammar_Notes: Polite business correspondence: 'Zögern Sie nicht mit...' or infinitive clause.

Meaning_EN: to attribute to / to trace back to
Example_German: Die Experten führen den Kursabsturz auf weltweite Unsicherheiten zurück.
Example_English: The experts trace the price crash back to global uncertainties.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb: 'etwas (Akk) zurückführen auf + Akk'. Causal attribution.

Meaning_EN: to agree on / to settle with (a person)
Example_German: Ich habe den genauen Liefertermin mit dem Spediteur ausgemacht.
Example_English: I settled on the exact delivery date with the freight forwarder.

Meaning_EN: to vouch for / to guarantee
Example_German: Der wohlhabende Onkel bürgt für den Bankkredit seines Neffen.
Example_English: The wealthy uncle vouches for his nephew's bank loan.

Meaning_EN: to serve as (a role or substitute)
Example_German: Das bequeme Sofa dient nachts als gemütliches Gästebett.
Example_English: The comfortable couch serves as a cozy guest bed at night.
Grammar_Notes: 'Als' takes Nominative agreeing with the subject.

Meaning_EN: to serve for / to be used for (purpose)
Example_German: Dieses spezielle Werkzeug dient zu schnellen Öffnen von Dosen.
Example_English: This special tool serves for opening cans quickly.

Meaning_EN: to be suitable for (a target audience or role)
Example_German: Dieses spannende Buch eignet sich hervorragend für Sprachanfänger.
Example_English: This exciting book is wonderfully suitable for language beginners.

Meaning_EN: to be suitable for (an action or function)
Example_German: Das robuste Holz eignet sich bestens zu Bau von Gartenmöbeln.
Example_English: The sturdy wood is best suited for building garden furniture.
Grammar_Notes: Task or utility suitability (often nominalized verbs: zum Kochen, zum Bau).

Meaning_EN: to be disgusted by / repulsed by
Example_German: Er ekelt sich furchtbar vor kriechenden Würmern.
Example_English: He is terribly disgusted by crawling worms.

Meaning_EN: to haggle / bargain over
Example_German: Auf dem bunten Trödelmarkt feilscht man gern um jeden einzelnen Euro.
Example_English: At the colorful flea market, people gladly haggle over every single euro.

Meaning_EN: to flee from / to escape from
Example_German: Tausende Menschen flohen vor den verheerenden Flammen des Waldbrands.
Example_English: Thousands of people fled from the devastating flames of the wildfire.

Meaning_EN: to get into / to fall into (trouble, panic, danger)
Example_German: Das Unternehmen geriet durch Fehlinvestitionen in große finanzielle Not.
Example_English: The company got into great financial distress through bad investments.
Grammar_Notes: Unintentionally entering a difficult state (in Panik geraten, in Wut geraten). Takes Akkusativ.

Meaning_EN: to prevent from / to hinder from
Example_German: Starker Nebel hinderte die Piloten an einem sicheren Landeanflug.
Example_English: Heavy fog prevented the pilots from a safe landing approach.

Meaning_EN: to be ashamed in front of (a person)
Example_German: Das Mädchen schämte sich vor den fremden Gästen und versteckte sich.
Example_English: The girl was ashamed in front of the unfamiliar guests and hid.
Grammar_Notes: Person in whose presence one feels ashamed takes 'vor + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: to be ashamed of (an action or behavior)
Example_German: Er schämte sich zutiefst für seine ungehobelten Worte.
Example_English: He was deeply ashamed of his rude words.

Meaning_EN: to be based on / to rest upon (facts, principles)
Example_German: Die wissenschaftliche These beruht auf verlässlichen Experimenten.
Example_English: The scientific thesis is based on reliable experiments.
Grammar_Notes: Takes Dativ (unlike 'hoffen auf' or 'warten auf'!). Formal and academic.

Meaning_EN: to be based on
Example_German: Der erfolgreiche Film basiert auf einer wahren Begebenheit.
Example_English: The successful movie is based on a true story.
Grammar_Notes: Takes Dativ ('auf + Dat'). Very common in journalism and academia.

Meaning_EN: to tie in with / to build upon (earlier progress/ideas)
Example_German: Wir möchten heute direkt an die Diskussion der letzten Woche anknüpfen.
Example_English: Today we would like to tie directly into last week's discussion.

Meaning_EN: to coordinate / tune / tailor to
Example_German: Das Vier-Gänge-Menü ist exakt auf die erlesenen Weine abgestimmt.
Example_English: The four-course menu is precisely matched to the exquisite wines.
Grammar_Notes: Harmonizing or tailoring one element to another.

Meaning_EN: to vote on (a motion or proposal)
Example_German: Die Vereinsmitglieder stimmen heute über den neuen Mitgliedsbeitrag ab.
Example_English: The club members are voting today on the new membership fee.

Meaning_EN: to stimulate / prompt / inspire to
Example_German: Das nachdenkliche Theaterstück regte die Zuschauer zu langen Diskussionen an.
Example_English: The thoughtful play stimulated the audience to long discussions.
Grammar_Notes: Incentivizing thought or action (anregen zum Nachdenken).

Meaning_EN: to call upon / urge / request someone to
Example_German: Die Flugbegleiterin forderte die Passagiere zu Anschnallen auf.
Example_English: The flight attendant called upon passengers to fasten their seatbelts.

Meaning_EN: to persist in / to stubbornly insist on
Example_German: Er beharrte stur auf seiner einmal gefassten Meinung.
Example_English: He stubbornly persisted in his once-formed opinion.
Grammar_Notes: Takes Dativ ('auf + Dat'). Connotes obstinacy or unwavering persistence.

Meaning_EN: to envy for
Example_German: Viele seiner Kollegen beneiden ihn um seine beneidenswerte Gelassenheit.
Example_English: Many of his colleagues envy him for his enviable serenity.

Meaning_EN: to press for / to urge (a quick decision or action)
Example_German: Die Kunden drängen ungeduldig auf eine rasche Behebung der Störung.
Example_English: The customers are impatiently pressing for a prompt resolution to the outage.

Meaning_EN: to compete for / to vie for
Example_German: Die begabten Athleten wetteifern ehrgeizig um den ersten Platz.
Example_English: The talented athletes ambitiously vie for first place.
Grammar_Notes: Elevated vocabulary for fierce competition over an accolade.

Meaning_EN: to admit to / to qualify for (an exam or study program)
Example_German: Nach Prüfung der Unterlagen wurde sie zu den Staatsprüfungen zugelassen.
Example_English: After reviewing the documents, she was admitted to the state examinations.

Meaning_EN: to shrink back from / to recoil from (a danger or obstacle)
Example_German: Ein entschlossener Bergsteiger schreckt nicht vor großen Gefahren zurück.
Example_English: A determined mountaineer does not shrink back from great dangers.
Grammar_Notes: Hesitating or shrinking from daunting tasks.

Meaning_EN: to keep from / to deter from
Example_German: Nichts auf der Welt konnte ihn von seinen ehrgeizigen Plänen abhalten.
Example_English: Nothing in the world could deter him from his ambitious plans.

Meaning_EN: to call for / to appeal for (action, donations)
Example_German: Der Bürgermeister rief die Bürger zu gegenseitiger Solidarität auf.
Example_English: The mayor appealed to citizens for mutual solidarity.

Meaning_EN: to invoke / to appeal to / to cite (a law, right, statement)
Example_German: Der Angeklagte berief sich vor Gericht auf sein Recht zu schweigen.
Example_English: The defendant invoked his right to remain silent in court.
Grammar_Notes: Legal or formal citation of authority or rights. Takes Akkusativ.

Meaning_EN: to interfere in / to meddle in
Example_German: Bitte mische dich nicht ungefragt in meine privaten Angelegenheiten ein!
Example_English: Please do not meddle unasked in my private affairs!
Grammar_Notes: Separable reflexive verb: sich ein|mischen in + Akk.

Meaning_EN: to reach for / to grasp at
Example_German: Das Kleinkind griff neugierig nach der glänzenden Tasse.
Example_English: The toddler curiously reached for the shiny mug.

Meaning_EN: to resort to / to reach for (measures, remedies)
Example_German: In seiner Verzweiflung griff er zu unkonventionellen Mitteln.
Example_English: In his desperation, he resorted to unconventional means.
Grammar_Notes: Choosing a remedy or extreme measure.

Meaning_EN: to be liable for / to be responsible for
Example_German: Eltern haften bekanntlich für die Schäden ihrer minderjährigen Kinder.
Example_English: Parents are famously liable for the damages of their minor children.
Grammar_Notes: Classic legal warning phrase in Germany ('Eltern haften für ihre Kinder').

Meaning_EN: to tend to / to have an inclination toward
Example_German: Unter starkem Stress neigt er leider zu voreiligen Kurzschlusshandlungen.
Example_English: Under severe stress he unfortunately tends toward hasty rash actions.

Meaning_EN: to have a crush on / to be fond of / to adore
Example_German: Als Teenager schwärmte sie heimlich für einen berühmten Popstar.
Example_English: As a teenager, she secretly had a crush on a famous pop star.

Meaning_EN: to rave about / to swoon over
Example_German: Sie schwärmt unaufhörlich von den kulinarischen Genüssen in Rom.
Example_English: She raves incessantly about the culinary delights in Rome.

Meaning_EN: to pass on to / to transition to (the next agenda item)
Example_German: Lassen Sie uns nun zu dem nächsten Tagesordnungspunkt übergehen.
Example_English: Let us now transition to the next agenda item.
Grammar_Notes: Separable verb: 'über|gehen zu + Dat' in meetings and presentations.

Meaning_EN: to entice / mislead / induce into
Example_German: Schlechte Vorbilder verleiteten den Jungen zu gefährlichen Mutproben.
Example_English: Bad role models enticed the boy into dangerous tests of courage.

Meaning_EN: dissatisfied with / unhappy with
Example_German: Viele Kunden sind unzufrieden mit dem langsamen Service.
Example_English: Many customers are dissatisfied with the slow service.

Meaning_EN: satisfied with / content with
Example_German: Der Chef ist sehr zufrieden mit deinen guten Arbeitsergebnissen.
Example_English: The boss is very satisfied with your good work results.
Grammar_Notes: Always takes 'mit + Dativ'. Essential everyday expression.

Meaning_EN: proud of
Example_German: Die Eltern sind unheimlich stolz auf ihre fleißige Tochter.
Example_English: The parents are incredibly proud of their hardworking daughter.

Meaning_EN: important for / to
Example_German: Ausreichend Schlaf ist enorm wichtig für die Konzentration.
Example_English: Sufficient sleep is enormously important for concentration.
Grammar_Notes: Takes 'für + Akkusativ' (or a plain Dativ pronoun: 'Das ist mir wichtig').

Meaning_EN: interested in
Example_German: Sind Sie an einem unverbindlichen Beratungsgespräch interessiert?
Example_English: Are you interested in a non-binding consultation?
Grammar_Notes: ATTENTION: 'interessiert sein an + Dativ' vs. the verb 'sich interessieren für + Akkusativ'!

Meaning_EN: grateful for / thankful for
Example_German: Ich bin dir unendlich dankbar für deine uneigennützige Hilfe.
Example_English: I am endlessly grateful to you for your unselfish help.
Grammar_Notes: Formula: jemandem (Dat) für etwas (Akk) dankbar sein.

Meaning_EN: angry with / mad at (a PERSON)
Example_German: Bist du immer noch böse auf deinen kleinen Bruder?
Example_English: Are you still mad at your little brother?

Meaning_EN: upset about / angry about (a SITUATION or outcome)
Example_German: Er war sehr böse über die unnötige Niederlage im Spiel.
Example_English: He was very upset about the unnecessary defeat in the game.

Meaning_EN: furious about (a MATTER or situation)
Example_German: Die Bürger sind wütend über die erneute Erhöhung der Ticketpreise.
Example_English: Citizens are furious about the renewed increase in ticket prices.

Meaning_EN: furious at / enraged with (a PERSON)
Example_German: Sie ist furchtbar wütend auf ihren unzuverlässigen Nachbarn.
Example_English: She is terribly furious at her unreliable neighbor.

Meaning_EN: glad about / happy about
Example_German: Wir sind alle sehr froh über die erfreulichen Nachrichten.
Example_English: We are all very glad about the pleasing news.

Meaning_EN: happy about / delighted with
Example_German: Sie ist überglücklich über das bestandene Vorstellungsgespräch.
Example_English: She is overjoyed about the passed job interview.

Meaning_EN: sad about
Example_German: Das Kind war untröstlich und traurig über den Verlust des Spielzeugs.
Example_English: The child was inconsolable and sad about the loss of the toy.

Meaning_EN: finished with / done with
Example_German: Bist du schon fertig mit deinen Hausaufgaben?
Example_English: Are you already finished with your homework?
Grammar_Notes: Completion of a task or parting with someone ('Ich bin fertig mit ihm').

Meaning_EN: in love with
Example_German: Romeo war unsterblich in Julia verliebt.
Example_English: Romeo was hopelessly in love with Juliet.

Meaning_EN: married to
Example_German: Mein Onkel ist seit über dreißig Jahren mit einer Ärztin verheiratet.
Example_English: My uncle has been married to a doctor for over thirty years.
Grammar_Notes: Always takes 'mit + Dativ' (in German you are married 'with' someone).

Meaning_EN: friends with
Example_German: Sie ist seit der Schulzeit eng mit meiner Schwester befreundet.
Example_English: She has been close friends with my sister since school days.

Meaning_EN: related to
Example_German: Ist er eigentlich über drei Ecken mit dir verwandt?
Example_English: Is he actually distantly related to you?

Meaning_EN: dependent on
Example_German: Unsere Pläne sind völlig abhängig von der aktuellen Wetterlage.
Example_English: Our plans are completely dependent on the current weather situation.

Meaning_EN: independent of / regardless of
Example_German: Das Gesetz gilt für alle Bürger, ganz unabhängig von ihrem Einkommen.
Example_English: The law applies to all citizens, quite independent of their income.
Grammar_Notes: Takes 'von + Dativ'. Frequently used as an adverb ('unabhängig davon').

Meaning_EN: reliant on / dependent upon
Example_German: Ohne Auto ist man auf dem Lande auf öffentliche Verkehrsmittel angewiesen.
Example_English: Without a car, one is reliant on public transport in the countryside.

Meaning_EN: ready for (an upcoming event, journey, or challenge)
Example_German: Bist du schon startklar und bereit für die große Reise?
Example_English: Are you already set and ready for the big journey?

Meaning_EN: ready for / willing to do (an action or compromise)
Example_German: Beide Parteien waren erfreulicherweise zu einem Kompromiss bereit.
Example_English: Fortunately, both parties were ready for a compromise.
Grammar_Notes: Willingness to take an action: 'zu + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: known among / well-known to (a group of people)
Example_German: Der junge Autor ist vor allem bei jugendlichen Lesern bekannt.
Example_English: The young author is particularly well-known among teenage readers.
Grammar_Notes: Audience or circle of familiarity: 'bei + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: known for / famous for (a quality, product, or feature)
Example_German: München ist weltweit bekannt für das berühmte Oktoberfest.
Example_English: Munich is known worldwide for the famous Oktoberfest.

Meaning_EN: popular with / liked by
Example_German: Die freundliche Lehrerin ist überaus beliebt bei ihren Schülern.
Example_English: The friendly teacher is extremely popular with her students.
Grammar_Notes: The demographic or group takes 'bei + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: enthusiastic about / thrilled by
Example_German: Das Publikum war restlos begeistert von der grandiosen Aufführung.
Example_English: The audience was utterly thrilled by the magnificent performance.

Meaning_EN: famous for
Example_German: Die Schweiz ist weltberühmt für ihre feine Schokolade und Uhren.
Example_English: Switzerland is world-famous for its fine chocolate and watches.

Meaning_EN: busy with / occupied with
Example_German: Er ist momentan vollauf mit den Vorbereitungen für die Messe beschäftigt.
Example_English: He is currently fully occupied with preparations for the trade fair.

Meaning_EN: involved in / participant in
Example_German: Mehrere renommierte Firmen sind an dem Großprojekt beteiligt.
Example_English: Several renowned companies are involved in the major project.

Meaning_EN: jealous of (in a relationship or affection)
Example_German: Er ist grundlos eifersüchtig auf jeden Mann, der sie anlächelt.
Example_English: He is groundlessly jealous of every man who smiles at her.

Meaning_EN: envious of (possessions, success, status)
Example_German: Niemand sollte neidisch auf den plötzlichen Erfolg anderer sein.
Example_English: Nobody should be envious of other people's sudden success.

Meaning_EN: in agreement with / agreed to
Example_German: Bist du mit dieser vorgeschlagenen Regelung einverstanden?
Example_English: Are you in agreement with this proposed regulation?

Meaning_EN: disappointed about (an EVENT, outcome, or fact)
Example_German: Sie war bitter enttäuscht über das schlechte Prüfungsergebnis.
Example_English: She was bitterly disappointed about the poor exam result.

Meaning_EN: disappointed in / by (a PERSON or their performance)
Example_German: Der Trainer war zutiefst enttäuscht von der lustlosen Mannschaft.
Example_English: The coach was deeply disappointed in the listless team.

Meaning_EN: determined to / resolved upon
Example_German: Die Regierung ist fest zu durchgreifenden Reformen entschlossen.
Example_English: The government is firmly resolved upon radical reforms.

Meaning_EN: astonished at / amazed by
Example_German: Wir waren sehr erstaunt über seine perfekten Deutschkenntnisse.
Example_English: We were very astonished at his perfect German skills.

Meaning_EN: capable of
Example_German: In einer Krise ist der Mensch oft zu ungeahnten Leistungen fähig.
Example_English: In a crisis, a person is often capable of unexpected achievements.

Meaning_EN: free from / free of
Example_German: Dieses Produkt ist garantiert frei von künstlichen Konservierungsstoffen.
Example_English: This product is guaranteed free of artificial preservatives.
Grammar_Notes: Absence of unwanted substances or burdens.

Meaning_EN: friendly to / kind towards
Example_German: Das Hotelpersonal war zu jeder Zeit überaus freundlich zu den Gästen.
Example_English: The hotel staff was extremely friendly to guests at all times.

Meaning_EN: polite to / courteous towards
Example_German: Ein Kellner sollte stets höflich zu allen Kunden sein.
Example_English: A waiter should always be polite to all customers.

Meaning_EN: strict with / stern towards
Example_German: Manche Eltern sind viel zu streng zu ihren heranwachsenden Kindern.
Example_English: Some parents are far too strict with their adolescent children.

Meaning_EN: suitable for (a target group or purpose)
Example_German: Diese Software ist besonders gut für kleine und mittlere Betriebe geeignet.
Example_English: This software is particularly well suited for small and medium-sized businesses.

Meaning_EN: eager to see / in suspense about / curious about (a future outcome)
Example_German: Ich bin schon unheimlich gespannt auf das morgige Endspiel!
Example_English: I am already incredibly curious/eager about tomorrow's final game!
Grammar_Notes: Anticipating a revelation or outcome. Always 'auf + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: used to / accustomed to
Example_German: Als Skandinavier ist er an eisige Winter gewöhnt.
Example_English: As a Scandinavian, he is used to freezing winters.

Meaning_EN: good at (a subject, discipline, or sport)
Example_German: Schon als Schüler war er außergewöhnlich gut in Mathematik.
Example_English: Even as a pupil he was exceptionally good at mathematics.
Grammar_Notes: Proficiency in a field takes 'in + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: kind to / good to (a person)
Example_German: Er war während der schweren Zeit immer gut zu mir.
Example_English: He was always kind to me during the difficult time.

Meaning_EN: bad at / poor in (a subject or skill)
Example_German: Leider bin ich ziemlich schlecht in Auswendiglernen von Jahreszahlen.
Example_English: Unfortunately, I am rather bad at memorizing dates.

Meaning_EN: curious about
Example_German: Die Kinder waren furchtbar neugierig auf die eingepackten Geschenke.
Example_English: The children were terribly curious about the wrapped gifts.

Meaning_EN: useful for
Example_German: Diese praktischen Tipps sind besonders nützlich für Sprachanfänger.
Example_English: These practical tips are particularly useful for language beginners.

Meaning_EN: open to (new ideas, suggestions)
Example_German: Unsere Abteilung ist jederzeit offen für innovative Vorschläge.
Example_English: Our department is always open to innovative suggestions.

Meaning_EN: rich in (vitamins, nutrients, minerals)
Example_German: Frische Beeren sind besonders reich an wertvollen Vitaminen.
Example_English: Fresh berries are particularly rich in valuable vitamins.
Grammar_Notes: Abundance of a resource takes 'an + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: poor in / low in
Example_German: Diese karge Wüstenregion ist extrem arm an Wasser und Vegetation.
Example_English: This barren desert region is extremely poor in water and vegetation.

Meaning_EN: harmful to / damaging to
Example_German: Plastikmüll im Meer ist extrem schädlich für die Tierwelt.
Example_English: Plastic waste in the ocean is extremely harmful to wildlife.

Meaning_EN: to blame for / at fault for
Example_German: Niemand von uns ist schuld an diesem unglücklichen Unfall.
Example_English: None of us is to blame for this unfortunate accident.
Grammar_Notes: Uninflected predicate adjective: 'schuld sein an + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: typical of
Example_German: Diese typische Gastfreundschaft ist bezeichnend für die Region.
Example_English: This typical hospitality is characteristic of the region.

Meaning_EN: convinced of
Example_German: Ich bin felsenfest von der Richtigkeit dieser Maßnahme überzeugt.
Example_English: I am rock-solidly convinced of the correctness of this measure.

Meaning_EN: responsible for
Example_German: Wer ist in Ihrer Abteilung verantwortlich für die IT-Sicherheit?
Example_English: Who in your department is responsible for IT security?

Meaning_EN: in charge of / responsible for (an administrative duty)
Example_German: Frau Müller ist für die Bearbeitung aller Visa-Anträge zuständig.
Example_English: Ms. Müller is in charge of processing all visa applications.

Meaning_EN: crazy about / mad about
Example_German: Die Kinder sind förmlich verrückt nach italienischem Schokoladeneis.
Example_English: The children are positively crazy about Italian chocolate ice cream.

Meaning_EN: concerned about / perturbed by (a political/economic situation)
Example_German: Die Ökonomen sind besorgt über die steigende Inflation.
Example_English: The economists are concerned about rising inflation.
Grammar_Notes: Concern regarding broader public issues: 'über + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: worried about (someone's safety, health, or welfare)
Example_German: Die Mutter war sehr besorgt um die Gesundheit ihres kranken Sohnes.
Example_English: The mother was very worried about the health of her sick son.
Grammar_Notes: Worry about personal well-being or safety: 'um + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: skeptical towards / about
Example_German: Die Anleger stehen dem neuen Finanzplan skeptisch gegenüberüber.
Example_English: Investors are skeptical towards the new financial plan.

Meaning_EN: open-minded towards / receptive to
Example_German: Sie zeigt sich sehr aufgeschlossen gegenüber fremden Kulturen gegenüber.
Example_English: She shows herself to be very open-minded towards foreign cultures.

Meaning_EN: distrustful of / suspicious towards
Example_German: Er war von Natur aus misstrauisch gegenüber Fremden gegenüber.
Example_English: He was by nature suspicious towards strangers.

Meaning_EN: sensitive to (cold, heat, light, criticism)
Example_German: Meine Zähne sind extrem empfindlich gegen Kälte und Säure.
Example_English: My teeth are extremely sensitive to cold and acid.

Meaning_EN: immune to (infection, criticism, charm)
Example_German: Nach der Impfung ist der Organismus immun gegen den Erreger.
Example_English: After the vaccination, the organism is immune to the pathogen.

Meaning_EN: allergic to (pollen, foods) / reacting badly to
Example_German: Sie reagiert stark allergisch auf Katzenhaare.
Example_English: She reacts severely allergic to cat hair.

Meaning_EN: caught off-guard by / surprised by (a person or unforeseen act)
Example_German: Der Torwart wurde völlig von dem weiten Schuss überrascht.
Example_English: The goalkeeper was completely surprised by the long shot.

Meaning_EN: surprised at / by (an outcome or fact)
Example_German: Alle waren positiv überrascht über die schnelle Genesung.
Example_English: Everyone was pleasantly surprised at the swift recovery.

Meaning_EN: full of / covered in
Example_German: Nach dem Waldspaziergang waren seine Schuhe voll von Schlamm.
Example_English: After the forest walk, his shoes were full of mud.
Grammar_Notes: Can also be used with plain Genitive ('voller Freude').

Meaning_EN: red with (anger, embarrassment, shame)
Example_German: Vor lauter Verlegenheit wurde der Junge knallrot vor Scham.
Example_English: Out of sheer embarrassment, the boy turned bright red with shame.
Grammar_Notes: Emotional involuntary physical reactions take 'vor + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: mute / speechless with (shock, astonishment)
Example_German: Die Zeugen blieben stumm vor Entsetzen über den Vorfall.
Example_English: The witnesses remained mute with horror at the incident.

Meaning_EN: pale with (fear, shock, envy)
Example_German: Er wurde kreidebleich und blass vor Angst vor der Prüfung.
Example_English: He turned chalk-white and pale with fear of the exam.

Meaning_EN: blind in (an eye - anatomical)
Example_German: Der alte Kater ist leider auf dem linken Auge völlig blind.
Example_English: The old tomcat is unfortunately completely blind in the left eye.
Grammar_Notes: Physical blindness in one eye: 'auf + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: blind to (faults, dangers, risks - figurative)
Example_German: Vor lauter Liebe war er blind für ihre vielen Fehler.
Example_English: Out of sheer love, he was blind to her many flaws.

Meaning_EN: deaf in (an ear - anatomical)
Example_German: Seit der Explosion ist der Soldat auf dem rechten Ohr taub.
Example_English: Since the explosion, the soldier has been deaf in his right ear.
Grammar_Notes: Physical deafness in an ear: 'auf + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: deaf to (arguments, advice - figurative)
Example_German: Der Diktator blieb taub für alle friedlichen Bitten des Volkes.
Example_English: The dictator remained deaf to all peaceful pleas of the people.

Meaning_EN: bitter about (injustice, life circumstances)
Example_German: Er war tief verbittert über die ungerechtfertigte Kündigung.
Example_English: He was deeply bitter about the unjustified dismissal.

Meaning_EN: exasperated / annoyed about
Example_German: Die Passagiere waren extrem verärgert über die stundenlange Verspätung.
Example_English: The passengers were extremely annoyed about the hours-long delay.

Meaning_EN: attentive to / aware of / alerted to
Example_German: Die Polizei wurde durch einen anonymen Hinweis auf das Versteck aufmerksam.
Example_English: The police became aware of the hideout through an anonymous tip.

Meaning_EN: hungry for / craving (success, news, power)
Example_German: Die junge Athletin ist hungrig nach neuen Rekorden und Siegen.
Example_English: The young athlete is hungry for new records and victories.

Meaning_EN: thirsty for (knowledge, justice, revenge)
Example_German: Wissenschaftler sind stets durstig nach neuen Erkenntnissen.
Example_English: Scientists are always thirsty for new insights.

Meaning_EN: addicted to
Example_German: Immer mehr Jugendliche sind süchtig nach sozialen Medien.
Example_English: More and more teenagers are addicted to social media.

Meaning_EN: obsessed with (an idea, mission, perfection)
Example_German: Der Erfinder war förmlich besessen von seiner neuen Vision.
Example_English: The inventor was positively obsessed with his new vision.

Meaning_EN: pleased about / delighted with
Example_German: Wir waren außerordentlich erfreut über deinen überraschenden Besuch.
Example_English: We were extraordinarily pleased about your surprise visit.

Meaning_EN: perturbed about / alarmed at
Example_German: Die Bürger sind zutiefst beunruhigt über die zunehmende Kriminalität.
Example_English: Citizens are deeply perturbed about the increasing crime.

Meaning_EN: characteristic of
Example_German: Die spitzen Türme sind absolut charakteristisch für diese gotische Kathedrale.
Example_English: The pointed towers are absolutely characteristic of this Gothic cathedral.

Meaning_EN: decisive for / crucial to
Example_German: Gute Teamarbeit ist oft entscheidend für den Projekterfolg.
Example_English: Good teamwork is often decisive for project success.

Meaning_EN: braced for / prepared for (unpleasant news or hardship)
Example_German: Man muss im Leben auf alle bösen Überraschungen gefasst sein.
Example_English: One must be braced for all bad surprises in life.
Grammar_Notes: Formula: gefasst sein auf + Akk (prepared for negative eventualities).

Meaning_EN: kind to / nice to (a person)
Example_German: Sei bitte immer nett zu deinen jüngeren Geschwistern!
Example_English: Please always be nice to your younger siblings!

Meaning_EN: impressed by
Example_German: Die Prüfungskommission war sichtlich beeindruckt von ihrem fundierten Fachwissen.
Example_English: The examination board was visibly impressed by her sound specialist knowledge.

Meaning_EN: fascinated by
Example_German: Die Kinder waren völlig fasziniert von den bunten Fischen im Aquarium.
Example_English: The children were completely fascinated by the colorful fish in the aquarium.

Meaning_EN: experienced in / skilled at
Example_German: Sie ist außerordentlich erfahren in der Leitung internationaler Projekte.
Example_English: She is extraordinarily experienced in managing international projects.

Meaning_EN: safe from (danger, persecution, bad weather)
Example_German: In der gemütlichen Berghütte waren die Wanderer sicher vor dem Unwetter.
Example_English: In the cozy mountain hut, the hikers were safe from the storm.

Meaning_EN: protected from / shielded against
Example_German: Die sensible Elektronik ist gut vor Feuchtigkeit und Staub geschützt.
Example_English: The sensitive electronics are well protected from moisture and dust.

Meaning_EN: separated from
Example_German: Seit zwei Jahren lebt er getrennt von seiner Ehefrau.
Example_English: He has been living separated from his wife for two years.
Grammar_Notes: Physical or marital separation takes 'von + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: indifferent towards / unconcerned about
Example_German: Man darf dem Leid anderer Menschen niemals gegenüber gleichgültig sein.
Example_English: One must never be indifferent towards the suffering of other people.
Grammar_Notes: Takes 'gegenüber + Dativ'. Can appear before or after the dative noun.

Meaning_EN: powerless against
Example_German: Gegenüber extremen Naturgewalten ist der Mensch oft völlig machtlos gegen die Zerstörung.
Example_English: Against extreme forces of nature, man is often completely powerless against destruction.

Meaning_EN: horrified at / appalled at
Example_German: Die ganze Welt war entsetzt über das verheerende Erdbeben.
Example_English: The whole world was horrified at the devastating earthquake.

Meaning_EN: indignant at / outraged about
Example_German: Die Belegschaft war empört über die plötzliche Schließung des Werks.
Example_English: The workforce was outraged about the sudden closure of the plant.

Meaning_EN: longing for / yearning for
Example_German: Der Exilant sehnte sich und blickte sehnsüchtig nach seiner fernen Heimat.
Example_English: The exile looked with yearning toward his distant homeland.

Meaning_EN: fear of / anxiety about
Example_German: Viele Kinder haben große Angst vor der Dunkelheit.
Example_English: Many children have great fear of the dark.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'sich fürchten vor + Dat'. Always takes 'vor + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: hope for
Example_German: Die Patienten haben noch immer berechtigte Hoffnung auf eine baldige Genesung.
Example_English: The patients still have justified hope for a speedy recovery.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'hoffen auf + Akk'. Always takes 'auf + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: interest for / passion for
Example_German: Sein großes Interesse für fremde Sprachen zeigte sich schon früh.
Example_English: His great interest for foreign languages showed itself early.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'sich interessieren für + Akk'. Takes 'für + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: interest in (a field, topic, or person)
Example_German: Das allgemeine Interesse an erneuerbaren Energien wächst rasant.
Example_English: General interest in renewable energy is growing rapidly.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'interessiert sein an + Dat'. Takes 'an + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: enjoyment in / pleasure derived from (an activity or hobby)
Example_German: Er hat die Freude an der täglichen Musikarbeit nie verloren.
Example_English: He never lost the pleasure in his daily musical work.
Grammar_Notes: Deriving joy from doing something (Freude haben an + Dat).

Meaning_EN: gladness about / pleasure in (PRESENT/PAST event or gift)
Example_German: Die Freude über das unerwartete Geschenk stand ihm ins Gesicht geschrieben.
Example_English: The joy about the unexpected gift was written all over his face.
Grammar_Notes: Reaction to present/past: corresponds to 'sich freuen über + Akk'.

Meaning_EN: joy of anticipation / looking forward to (FUTURE event)
Example_German: Die Vorfreude und Freude auf das bevorstehende Weihnachtsfest war riesig.
Example_English: The anticipation and joy for the upcoming Christmas celebration was huge.
Grammar_Notes: Future anticipation: corresponds to 'sich freuen auf + Akk'.

Meaning_EN: question about / inquiry regarding
Example_German: Die Frage nach dem Sinn des Lebens beschäftigt Philosophen seit Jahrtausenden.
Example_English: The question about the meaning of life has occupied philosophers for millennia.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'fragen nach + Dat'. Always 'nach + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: answer to / response to
Example_German: Die Antwort auf diese schwierige Frage blieb er uns schuldig.
Example_English: He remained indebted to us for the answer to this difficult question.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'antworten auf + Akk'. Always 'auf + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: request for
Example_German: Seine Bitte um finanzielle Unterstützung wurde wohlwollend geprüft.
Example_English: His request for financial support was benevolently examined.

Meaning_EN: gratitude for / thanks for
Example_German: Als Dank für die Einladung brachte sie einen herrlichen Blumenstrauß mit.
Example_English: As thanks for the invitation, she brought along a wonderful bouquet of flowers.

Meaning_EN: congratulations on
Example_German: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zu deinem heutigen Geburtstag!
Example_English: Warm congratulations on your birthday today!
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'gratulieren zu + Dat'. Always 'zu + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: invitation to
Example_German: Vielen Dank für die freundliche Einladung zu deiner Hochzeit.
Example_English: Thank you very much for the kind invitation to your wedding.

Meaning_EN: doubt about
Example_German: Es gibt berechtigte Zweifel an der Glaubwürdigkeit des Zeugen.
Example_English: There are justified doubts about the witness's credibility.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'zweifeln an + Dat'. Always 'an + Dativ'.

Meaning_EN: criticism of
Example_German: Die scharfe Kritik an den neuen Sparmaßnahmen war unüberhörbar.
Example_English: The sharp criticism of the new austerity measures was unmistakable.
Grammar_Notes: Formula: Kritik an + Dat üben (to level criticism at).

Meaning_EN: memory of / reminder of
Example_German: Die lebendige Erinnerung an diesen Sommertag verblasste nie.
Example_English: The vivid memory of that summer day never faded.
Grammar_Notes: Corresponds to 'sich erinnern an + Akk'. Always 'an + Akkusativ'.

Meaning_EN: search for / quest for
